Subject: Cost qualification — monthly token profile & PO threshold

Hi Elena & team,

Thanks again for taking the call earlier — appreciated the clear context on expected call volumes across the triage and summarization flows. Quick recap and items I promised to follow up on: 

1) Token profile we discussed (monthly forecast):
   - Peak LLM tokens (inbound + generated): ~50M tokens/month (expected months 1-3)
   - Steady-state: 20–30M tokens/month after model tweaks and caching

2) Procurement / PO threshold question you raised:
   - Current internal PO approval trigger: $50k monthly or $600k annual (Elena, confirm if the $50k is PO minimum or approval band)

3) Unit economics (quick view):
   - Target we proposed on the call: $900–1,200 per 1M tokens depending on model variant and caching levels
   - Example scenarios included in the attached estimate (redwood_pricing_estimate_v1.pdf)

Next steps I recommend:
- Elena: confirm whether the $50k is a monthly trigger or a one-time procurement hurdle. Also please share the procurement contact and any required vendor paperwork.
- I'll loop in finance (Marissa) to confirm whether we can structure a pilot PO under $50k with month-to-month billing while procurement completes the annual contract.
- If you can confirm rough monthly spend band (best, expected, worst), I will send a short spreadsheet that maps those bands to recommended model variants and a projected $/1M tokens.

Attachments: redwood_pricing_estimate_v1.pdf (pdf) — quick tiered estimate; SOW_template_acme.docx (docx) — draft SOW we can adapt.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz

Thanks Vanessa — that was a helpful recap. A couple quick clarifications from my side before we bring procurement into the loop: 

- The $50k you referenced is our internal monthly approval threshold; any vendor spend expected to exceed that in a month requires VP sign-off. Smaller orders (~<$50k) can be handled by the procurement team directly but we prefer consolidated monthly billing.
- Our procurement contact is listed on the cc for visibility; they typically require a vendor questionnaire, W-9, and a proof of SOC2- or ISO-type controls.

Clarifying question on unit economics: the $900–1,200 / 1M tokens range — is that inclusive of embedding calls and reranking, or pure generation token pricing? We have a high embedding fan-out for retrieval so I want to make sure we model that. Also do you have a recommended starting model band if we were to cap spend at $40k/month for month 1 trial?

If you can send the band mapping spreadsheet you mentioned, I’ll route it to procurement and our VP for a quick look.

Best,
Elena Morales
Head of Conversational Products
Acme Health

Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 11:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Cost qualification — monthly token profile & PO threshold

Elena — great questions, thanks. Short answers up front then a simple band mapping attached.

- Pricing scope: the $900–1,200 / 1M tokens range is a blended generation price assuming caching and continuous-batching; embedding units are priced separately in the attached estimate. The attached PDF has line items for: text-gen, embeddings, and reranking.

- If you want to cap at ~$40k/month for a month-1 pilot, recommended configuration (conservative):
   * Model: rdx-medium-1 (quantized) for generation where latency sensitivity is moderate
   * Embeddings: rdx-embed-1 (batching every 30s) for lower cost — estimate ~8M embed tokens/month in your fan-out profile
   * Approx projected spend: $32k–$42k depending on actual fan-out and caching hit rates

- Attached mapping (also Sheet link in HubSpot): maps three monthly bands to model variants and projected $/1M tokens. Quick highlights:
   * Pilot band ($10k–$50k): aggressive caching + quantized model -> target $/1M ~ $750
   * Growth band ($50k–$150k): mixed models, reserved capacity option -> target $/1M ~ $600–800
   * Enterprise band (>$150k): dedicated capacity + SLOs -> target $/1M ~ $450–600

Procurement ask: given your internal $50k approval threshold, two options we typically recommend so procurement can move faster:
1) PO split approach — issue a pilot PO under $50k for month 1 (we invoice monthly) while procurement processes the annual commitment.
2) Letter of intent + master SOW — procurement issues a small initial PO to start work and we sign an MoU allowing us to commence technical onboarding.

Marissa & Aditya — pls confirm that finance can accept a month-to-month pilot PO under $50k while procurement completes vendor setup. If there are special billing terms (net 30 vs net 45) call them out.

Next: I’ll add the band mapping sheet to HubSpot and request a short procurement call (15 min) to move vendor setup along.

Attachments: redwood_pricing_estimate_v1.pdf, SOW_template_acme.docx

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
vanessa@redwood.ai

Subject: Internal: Please confirm pilot PO flow for Acme Health (re: Cost qualification)

Marissa / Aditya — looping you both as requested on the call. Quick summary and ask: 

- Prospect: Acme Health (Elena Morales). They have an internal monthly approval threshold of $50k. They’re willing to do a month-1 pilot ~$40k if procurement can process a small PO.
- Ask for Finance (Marissa): can we accept monthly invoicing for a pilot under $50k while procurement completes vendor onboarding for a larger annual contract? Also any constraints on net terms or billing entity naming that would block a small PO?
- Ask for SE (Aditya): can you confirm the conservative spend projection for the pilot configuration (rdx-medium-1 + rdx-embed-1) and any suggestions to tighten the $/1M token estimate (caching knobs, quantization tradeoffs)?

I’ve attached the pricing estimate we shared with the customer. If Finance can confirm acceptance of a pilot PO, I’ll propose option 1 (pilot PO under $50k) to procurement and schedule a 15-minute vendor onboarding call.

Thanks — Vanessa
